thread:
jess: Heads-up 1:30 UTC  customer ACME opened a ticket: CSV export of audit logs shows masked user IDs even though their org admin can see IDs in the console viewer. attaching customer snippet
mike: can you paste the CSV row they attached? any job-run errors?
jess: they sent this minimal CSV excerpt:
```
user_id,action,resource,timestamp
MASKED_abc123,access_grant,project/blue,2026-03-19T21:03:12Z
```
mike: odd. our export job returned 200 and job-run logs show complete stream write. implies masking happened during row serialization, not a storage issue.
sara: relevant context: last month we switched audit_event.user_id to be envelope-encrypted with a per-tenant KEK (tenant-specific SP key). If the caller cannot call KMS:Decrypt on that key, our display layer surfaces MASKED_* placeholders. That was intentional to avoid PII leaks.
jess: customer claims they can see full user_id when browsing the console viewer UI. export CSV masks instead. inconsistent UX.
sara: sounds like viewer flow is using backend-system decryption (system principal token), while export is attempting to respect caller credentials and failing decryption. I suspect export is running the KMS call with end-user creds, hence MASKED.
mike: confirmed: export pipeline uses the same rowfilter/rbac checks added during the rowfilter rewrite. We added defense-in-depth: export won't call KMS on behalf of a user unless they have explicit audit_decrypt permission. This might have broken implicit behavior for orgs that relied on console access.
tina: product perspective: customers expect parity between viewer and export. We need either parity or explicit visible differences (and warnings).
jess: security risk: if we change export to always decrypt with system principal then someone lacking RBAC could get PII in downloads. Need clear security sign-off and threat model review.
sara: check KMS logs: there are AccessDenied 403s for tenant keys from export attempts (example: ERROR: AccessDenied key=tenant-7890 caller=user:bob). So export is indeed attempting user-scoped decrypts.
mike: short-term mitigation idea: add an "export preflight" endpoint invoked by console before starting export. It would simulate decrypts and return which columns will be masked, plus reasons. UI shows modal listing masked columns and a checkbox to continue. Also log an audit event for the preflight result.
tina: that sounds good and low-risk. keeps current security model but improves transparency. customers can see why fields are masked.
mike: medium-term options we discussed internally:
- add server-side audited flow audit_export that runs decryption with system principal but enforces RBAC at row level; requires security review and probably new RBAC flags
- introduce a new permission grant audit.decrypt_export that org admins can assign to service tokens or roles
- augment export schema to include machine-readable meta columns like __masked_fields and __mask_reasons so downstream consumers can detect when data was intentionally redacted

jess: I propose we ship preflight + __masked_fields metadata as the quick win. Then evaluate audit.decrypt_export if customers need it.
sara: implementation notes: preflight will call the existing decrypt path in dry-run mode and return a per-record per-column result. I'll own the endpoint. ETA: 3 business days unless KMS rate limits are a surprise.
mike: I'll add schema metadata in the export job and ensure the export writer includes a JSON metadata footer or an extra column __masked_fields. ETA: 1 day. I'll also add a short-running CI regression that runs synthetic export and asserts PII not written to long-retention logs.
jess: ownership and timeline: sara -> preflight API + dry-run decrypt code; mike -> export schema + CI test; tina -> customer support copy + console modal copy; jess -> security review and final sign-off. Target dates: schema change by 2026-03-23, preflight API + modal by 2026-03-26.
tina: will draft comms for support and update docs; will include guidance for admins if they want exports to include decrypted IDs (policy + exact permission to grant).
sara: side note: we found two scheduled compliance exports last month that used system principal decrypts (approved legal requests). I'll tag those jobs in KMS logs with service:compliance to make them auditable.
devsec-bot: Reminder: run export-e2e regression with synthetic tenant and ensure no PII is stored in event logs beyond short retention. Also add KMS access pattern alert for unexpected decrypts. :robot_face:
mike: will follow up with regression and add an alert rule for anomalous system-principal decrypts.
jess: action items summarized in Jira: ENGSEC-1142 (preflight endpoint, sara), ENGSEC-1143 (export metadata + CI, mike), DOCS-432 (support template, tina). Security review slot booked for 2026-03-24.
sara: I'll include detail in PR about dry-run KMS call not issuing Decrypt requests in prod (it only simulates and uses KMS:CanDecrypt check where possible). If we must do real decrypts in preflight for accuracy we should ensure the call uses ephemeral system principal and is audited.
jess: final note: let's avoid any change that would silently escalate privileges. Preflight + visible masking metadata gives customers immediate clarity and reduces support noise. We'll revisit permission model if demand rises.
mike: agreed. I'll start the schema patch and add the __masked_fields column as a JSON array string.
tina: I'll post a short reply to ACME outlining the steps and ETA later today.
jess: thanks everyone. I'll update the ticket and ping ACME when we have the preflight modal mock.
